senses.en: a serious argument or disagreement
examples: The firm is involved in a legal [[dispute]] with its competitor.

senses.zh: 无可争辩的；不可否认的
senses.en: unable to be challenged or denied
examples: It is [[indisputable]] that the crime rate has been decreasing.

senses.en: a statement or account that makes sth. clear or easy to understand
examples: Could you give me a quick [[explanation]] of how the machine works?

senses.en: simple and easy to understand
examples: The question seemed [[straightforward]] enough.

senses.en: the study of the way in which money and goods are produced and used
the wealth that a country gets from business and industry
examples: The country's [[economy]] grew at an annual rate of more than 10 percent.

senses.en: firmly press sth., typically with your fingers
examples: As she waited for the interview, he [[squeezed]] her hand and wished her good luck.

senses.en: (~ sb. in sth.; ~ in sth.) make sb. take part in sth.; take part in sth.
examples: The two governments have agreed to [[engage]] in a dialogue to solve the problem.

senses.en: control or have a lot of influence over sb. / sth., esp. in an unpleasant way
examples: The industry is [[dominated]] by five multinational companies.

senses.en: use machines to make goods or materials, usu. in large numbers or amounts
examples: It is a company that [[manufactures]] drugs.

senses.en: the process of making goods or materials using machines, usu. in large numbers or amounts
examples: Cost will determine the methods of [[manufacture]].

senses.en: the process or business of producing goods in factories
examples: Thousands of jobs had been lost in [[manufacturing]].

senses.en: gather in crops
examples: Farmers here still plant and [[harvest]] their crops by hand.

senses.en: the process or period of gathering in crops
examples: The drought has made farmers anxious about the [[harvest]].

senses.en: (of fruit or crops) fully grown and ready to eat
examples: Those tomatoes aren't [[ripe]] yet —— they're still green.

senses.en: without limits, edges, or ends
examples: Her fellow members marveled at her seemingly [[infinite]] energy.

senses.en: very great in amount or degree
examples: There was an [[infinite]] variety of drinks to choose from.

senses.en: (of a message) being received rather than sent
examples: My email box is flooded with [[incoming]] messages when a school year begins.

senses.zh: 与移动电话等技术有关的
senses.en: relating to mobile phones and similar technology
examples: Over half of the country's e-commerce is now conducted on [[mobile]] devices.

senses.en: able to be moved from one place to another
examples: The seats in the classroom are not [[mobile]].

senses.en: deal with
examples: If you can't [[handle]] the job, I'll ask someone else to do it.

senses.en: a list of tasks that need to be done
examples: I'll take a moment away from my [[to-do list]] and think about my dream holiday.

senses.en: as is certain to happen
examples: One's accent [[inevitably]] gives away their place of origin.

senses.en: give too much of a thing to sb.
examples: We were [[overwhelmed]] by requests for information.

senses.zh: （感情上）使（某人）感到不能自持，使不知所措
senses.en: have a very strong emotional effect on sb.
examples: She was [[overwhelmed]] by the need to talk to someone.

senses.en: having a definite limit or fixed size
examples: Every computer has a [[finite]] amount of memory.

senses.en: show or prove sth. clearly
examples: Hitchcock's films [[demonstrate]] that a British filmmaker could learn from Hollywood.

senses.zh: （情况）出乎意料的，令人啼笑皆非的
senses.en: (of a situation) strange or amusing because it is very different from what you expect
examples: It's [[ironic]] that she became a teacher —— she used to hate school.

senses.en: a person who studies or writes about economics
a situation in which there is not enough of sth.
examples: Many college graduates hunt for jobs in large cities owing to the [[scarcity]] of opportunities in small towns.

senses.zh: 已承诺（或同意）的事；不得不做的事
senses.en: sth. that you have promised or agreed to do, or that you have to do
examples: Women often have to strike a balance between work and their family [[commitments]].

senses.en: a promise to do sth. or to behave in a particular way
examples: Alice doesn't want to make a big emotional [[commitment]] to Steve at the moment.

senses.zh: 优先处理的事；当务之急
senses.en: the thing that you think is most important and that needs attention before anything else
examples: The customer is high on our list of [[priority]].

senses.en: (AmE prioritize) treat sth. as being more important than other things
examples: The company has failed to [[prioritise]] safety.

senses.en: (AmE prioritize) determine the order for dealing with a series of items or tasks according to their relative importance
examples: You should make a list of all the jobs you have to do and [[prioritise]] them.

senses.en: extremely important because it will affect other things
examples: This aid money is [[crucial]] to the government's economic policies.

senses.en: make sb. share a particular feeling
examples: The panic in the mother's voice [[infected]] her children.

senses.en: give sb. a disease
examples: People with the virus may feel perfectly well, but they can still [[infect]] others.

senses.en: free time
examples: Most people only have a limited amount of [[leisure]] time.

senses.en: the process of improving or becoming stronger again
examples: The economy is showing signs of [[recovery]].

senses.en: a return to a normal state of health, mind, or strength
examples: It is hoped that Lawrence can make a full [[recovery]] from the operation.

senses.en: a sudden increase in the number of times that sth. bad happens
examples: Can anything be done about this unhappiness [[epidemic]]?

senses.en: a widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community at a particular time
examples: A flu [[epidemic]] is sweeping through the United States this winter.

senses.en: being the best or most extreme example of its kind
examples: This race will be the [[ultimate]] test of your skill.

senses.en: happening at the end of a long process
examples: My manager will make the [[ultimate]] decision about whom to employ.

senses.en: the social or professional position of sb. / sth. in relation to others
examples: Doctors have traditionally enjoyed high social [[status]].

senses.en: sth. that shows a particular quality
examples: His gun was a [[badge]] of power for him.

senses.en: a small piece of metal, cloth, plastic with a picture or words on it, worn to show rank, membership of a group, support for a political idea, etc.
examples: He pulled out a [[badge]] and said he was a police officer.

senses.en: sth. that can be regarded as a sign of sth. else
examples: All the main economic [[indicators]] suggest that trade is improving.

senses.en: completely stupid or unreasonable
examples: It seems quite [[absurd]] to expect anyone to drive for three hours just for a 20-minute meeting.

senses.en: an amount of money paid for a piece of work or a service
examples: Does the bank charge a [[fee]] for setting up an account?

senses.en: (not in passive) say that you are annoyed, not satisfied, or unhappy about sth./ sb.
examples: Residents are [[complaining]] because traffic in this area has increased.

senses.en: get back sth. you no longer have, esp. an ability or a quality
examples: She paused on the edge, trying to [[regain]] her balance.

senses.en: (~ to) the means or opportunity to approach or enter a place
examples: The police managed to gain [[access]] to the house through an upstairs window.

senses.en: walk somewhere in a slow, relaxed way
examples: We were [[strolling]] along, laughing and joking.

senses.en: without hurrying
examples: We walked [[leisurely]] into the hotel.

senses.en: unhurried or relaxed
examples: After getting up, we had a [[leisurely]] breakfast at our hotel.

senses.en: cruel or violent treatment of sb.
examples: The woman suffered years of physical [[abuse]].

senses.en: (infml.) a person who is not strong, brave, or confident
examples: The more she called her son a [[wimp]], the less confident he became.

senses.en: (AmE baggage) the cases, bags, etc. that you carry when you are traveling
examples: We dropped our [[luggage]] off at our hotel and went sightseeing.

senses.en: almost
examples: She blamed me for [[practically]] every mistake in the report.

senses.zh: 无谓的激动（或忧虑、活动）；大惊小怪
senses.en: unnecessary excitement, worry, or activity
examples: We tried to arrange a ceremony with as little [[fuss]] as possible.

senses.en: become or make sth. full of folds or lines
examples: My dress got all [[crushed]] in my suitcase.

senses.en: press or squeeze sth. so hard that it is damaged or injured, or loses its shape
examples: The car was completely [[crushed]] under the truck.

senses.en: the type of person you are, including your character, your typical behavior, your abilities, etc.
examples: Paula seemed to be her usual cheerful [[self]] a week after she came back home.

senses.en: a secret plan made by two or more people to do sth. harmful or illegal
examples: He was charged with [[conspiracy]] to commit criminal damage.

senses.en: a company that takes passengers and goods to different places by plane
examples: I won't fly with an [[airline]] that has a bad safety record.

senses.zh: （尤指在社交场合）使尴尬，使窘迫
senses.en: make sb. feel ashamed, nervous, or uncomfortable, esp. in front of other people
examples: He didn't want to [[embarrass]] her by asking questions.

senses.en: a feeling of being nervous or ashamed because of what people know or think about you
examples: She suffered extreme [[embarrassment]] at not knowing how to read and write.

senses.en: shy, awkward, or ashamed, esp. in a social situation
examples: The girl felt [[embarrassed]] at being the center of attention.

senses.en: a long narrow passage on a train or between rooms in a building, with doors on one or both sides
examples: We had to wait outside in the [[corridor]] until our names were called.

senses.en: trip or momentarily lose one's balance; almost fall
examples: Victor [[stumbled]] over the step as he came in.

senses.zh: 使用，占用（空间、面积、时间等）
senses.en: fill or use a space, an area, or an amount of time
examples: The bed seemed to [[occupy]] most of the room.

senses.en: live or stay in a place
examples: He [[occupies]] the house without paying any rent.

senses.zh: 空着的；闲置的；无人占用的
senses.en: empty, with nobody living there or using it
examples: I sat down at the nearest [[unoccupied]] table in the restaurant.

senses.zh: （做困难或不愉快的事情所需要的）勇气，魄力，决心
senses.en: (~s) (infml.) the courage and determination you need to do sth. difficult or unpleasant
examples: When failure knocks you down, will you have the [[guts]] to get up and get going?

senses.en: say sth. quickly in an angry way
examples: There's no need to [[snap]] at me — it's not my fault that you lost your wallet.

senses.en: break or cause to break suddenly and completely, typically with a sharp cracking sound
examples: You'll [[snap]] that ruler if you bend it too far.

senses.en: (infml.) take a photograph
examples: Dave [[snapped]] a picture of me and Lucas.

senses.en: the length of time that sb. lives or that sth. lasts
examples: That large sum of money will last me a [[lifetime]].

senses.en: manage to find time for sb. / sth. although you are very busy
examples: How can you manage to [[squeeze in]] so much work?

senses.en: do an amount of work
examples: We've got a lot of work to [[get through]] today.

senses.en: make sb. feel worried and upset
examples: The CEO felt [[weighed down]] by his responsibilities.

senses.en: undertake a task or responsibility, esp. a difficult one
examples: Don't [[take on]] too much work — the extra cash isn't worth it.

senses.zh: （尤指经历一系列意外后）最终处于，到头来
senses.en: be in a particular situation, state, or place after a series of events, esp. when you did not plan it
examples: He came round for a coffee and we [[ended up]] having a meal together.

senses.en: add sth. at no extra cost
examples: Buy this book and we [[throw in]] a CD.

senses.en: to some degree, but not completely
examples: Their harmonious relationship resulted [[in part]] from their similar goals.

senses.en: (of an aircraft, etc.) leave the ground and begin to fly
examples: I felt quite excited when the plane [[took off]] from Heathrow.

senses.en: complain or become angry about sth., esp. when this is not necessary
examples: The soup is just a bit salty. I don't know why you're [[making]] such [[a fuss about]] it.

senses.zh: 到达（尤指有人在等候之处）
senses.en: arrive, esp. at the place where sb. is waiting for you
examples: We had 200 people [[show up]] for the conference.

senses.zh: （尤指在困难情况下）准时到达，赶上
senses.en: succeed in getting somewhere in time for sth. or when this is difficult
examples: You can still [[make it]] to the railway station if you set out right away.

senses.en: before sth. happens or is expected to happen
examples: I should warn you [[in advance]] that I'm not a very good dancer.
